traditions.cautions: Kolam is a daily ritual offering (to Bhudevi / threshold deities) and is strongly gendered (women's practice); it is shared across Tamil-speaking regions and diaspora, so attribute it to the Tamil tradition rather than a single state. Avoid presenting generated outputs as ritual kolams; use 'inspired by the Tamil kolam tradition'. Do not combine with deity imagery.

traditions.name: Kolam (pulli / sikku kolam)

traditions.cautions: The jilan/jilang pulye and jig-jiro are priestly ceremonial shawls said to carry supernatural power and worn at Myoko, Murung and Subu rituals; the jikhe tarii and certain skirts mark social position and ceremonial status. Frame any design as 'inspired by Apatani band and lozenge weaving', never as a reproduction of a named priestly shawl. The GI is held by a producer company (Zeet Zeero), not the community as a whole.
motif_vocabulary: Formal arrangements of lines and bands (yellow and blue lines on everyday shawls)

rows of dark-blue diamonds flanked by red and yellow horizontal stripes (jikhe tarii jacket)
white shawl with black lozenge motifs and dots all over (jikhe pulye)
black shawl with central lengthwise white/orange band and blue side stripes, lozenge-and-dot ends (jilang pulye). IGNCA adds upright and pendent triangles, herringbone, frets
genuine spirals occur only on the priest's shawl.
traditions.name: Apatani textiles (banded shawls, three-band skirts, lozenge-row jackets)

traditions.cautions: These are Indo-Islamic funerary and religious monuments (Salim Chishti's dargah is an active Sufi shrine where pilgrims tie threads to the jalis). Use 'inspired by Mughal jaali geometry', never reproduce or name a specific shrine screen as the product. Jaali geometry is shared across the Islamic world; do not claim UP-exclusive origin. Many UP jalis (e.g. Taj cenotaph screen) are floral/inlaid rather than purely geometric; brief should target the geometric type.
motif_vocabulary: Regular geometric tilings cut as holes in a solid panel: hexagon/six-pointed-star nets, octagon-and-cross, squares-and-rhombi, interlaced polygons
floral/arabesque jalis also exist (Salim Chishti) but the verifiable target here is the geometric type
traditions.name: Mughal pierced-stone jaali screens of Agra and Fatehpur Sikri

traditions.cautions: Kolam is a daily ritual offering (to Bhudevi / threshold deities) and is strongly gendered (women's practice); it is shared across Tamil-speaking regions and diaspora, so attribute it to the Tamil tradition rather than a single state. traditions.cautions: Largely sacred architectural ornament (temples, also churches and a mosque); many murals are damaged or whitewashed and the practice nearly died out. traditions.cautions: The Nicobarese are a Scheduled Tribe in a restricted-access area and the GI is held by a tribal cooperative; any brief must say 'inspired by plaited pandanus mat structure' and must not claim to be a Nicobari mat or use the names Chatrai/Hileuoi as a product name. The mat has ceremonial use (serving food at festivals, hospitality). Do not extend this to other island communities: nothing from Jarawa, Sentinelese, Onge, Great Andamanese or Shompen material culture is proposed or appropriate.
motif_vocabulary: GI Journal 193: 'The weaving process involves crisscrossing the dried leaves by hand, creating a unique, attractive texture ... with different designs and patterns depending on the mat's intended use'

mats are double-layered, typically 6 x 3 ft, natural brownish colour, no artificial colours. Global InCH: 'light and dark leaves are interwoven to create intricate patterns'. Specific pattern names are not documented in any source fetched.

traditions.cautions: Kolam is a daily ritual offering (to Bhudevi / threshold deities) and is strongly gendered (women's practice); it is shared across Tamil-speaking regions and diaspora, so attribute it to the Tamil tradition rather than a single state. Avoid presenting generated outputs as ritual kolams; use 'inspired by the Tamil kolam tradition'. Do not combine with deity imagery.
motif_vocabulary: Closed looping curves drawn around a lattice of dots (pulli)
in sikku kolam one or more continuous lines encircle every dot and cross 'over and under'
line kolams join adjacent dots into geometric figures (stars, lotuses, lamps).
traditions.name: Kolam (pulli / sikku kolam)

traditions.cautions: Sacred ritual art: the kalam is consecrated, worshipped and ritually erased; most kalams are deity images drawn by hereditary specialist communities. Crosswise: two 2.5 in black woollen bands (Hruih) dividing the puan into three, and seven ~1 in deep-red woollen bands at the two ends with thin green, yellow, blue and pink lines between

traditions.cautions: Strong caution. Chakhesang shawls are GI-protected and community-owned; the Chakhesang Women Welfare Society sued a designer and TRIFED in 2020 over misuse. Many shawls encode earned status (Thupikhu/Hapidasa for Feast-of-Merit couples), are gendered (Rira men, Rura women), and some are reserved for funerals; wearing an unearned shawl is taboo. Never reproduce a named shawl's identity or its figurative motifs (mithun, elephant, spear, shield); generate only abstract band-and-square compositions 'inspired by Chakhesang band geometry'. Red dyeing is traditionally restricted to elder women.
motif_vocabulary: GI journal 97 specifies 14+ shawl types by band geometry, e.g. Rira: red ground, four black bands each 11.5 cm wide divided by 2 cm red lines, red side bands 16 cm, a central row of 2 cm white squares in a 2 cm band, and borders of small white squares on a thin black row at each selvedge
Rura: red ground with white bands (14 cm side bands), white squares 3.5 cm

other types: black with white and red stripes, black with orange bands 15-17 cm, black with a series of white dots down the centre, dark blue with alternate 7-8 cm red bands and thin white stripes carrying 6-dot flower patterns, white ground with red and blue bands (band spacing ~4 cm, 3 cm white lines)
traditions.name: Chakhesang shawls (banded Naga shawls with square-row centres)

traditions.cautions: These are Indo-Islamic funerary and religious monuments (Salim Chishti's dargah is an active Sufi shrine where pilgrims tie threads to the jalis). Use 'inspired by Mughal jaali geometry', never reproduce or name a specific shrine screen as the product. Jaali geometry is shared across the Islamic world; do not claim UP-exclusive origin. Many UP jalis (e.g. Taj cenotaph screen) are floral/inlaid rather than purely geometric; brief should target the geometric type.
motif_vocabulary: Regular geometric tilings cut as holes in a solid panel: hexagon/six-pointed-star nets, octagon-and-cross, squares-and-rhombi, interlaced polygons
floral/arabesque jalis also exist (Salim Chishti) but the verifiable target here is the geometric type
traditions.name: Mughal pierced-stone jaali screens of Agra and Fatehpur Sikri

traditions.cautions: Ritual art tied to Hindu pujas, births, sacred-thread and marriage rites and to specific deities (Nav Durga, Saraswati, Shiva, Lakshmi); swastik is a sacred auspicious symbol here and must not be rendered in a way that resembles the Nazi hakenkreuz; avoid naming a specific deity chauki as a product; use 'inspired by Kumaoni aipan geometry'. GI-protected name 'Uttarakhand Aipan' should not be used as a product label. Made by women; attribute accordingly.
motif_vocabulary: Chauki (seat) diagrams: Nav Durga chauki = three horizontal and three vertical lines with a swastik at centre and nine dots
Chamunda Hast chauki = two triangles crossed by two diagonals with a five-pointed star inside a circle, circle ringed by eight lotus petals
Saraswati chauki = five-pointed star with swastik/lamp at centre
Janeu chauki = seven stars within a six-sided figure
Shiv peeth = eight-cornered figure with 12 dots joined by 12 lines
borders of vasudhara (vertical dripped lines), dots, lotus (ashtadal kamal), Lakshmi footprints
traditions.name: Aipan (Kumaoni ritual floor and wall painting)

traditions.cautions: Ritual art tied to Hindu pujas, births, sacred-thread and marriage rites and to specific deities (Nav Durga, Saraswati, Shiva, Lakshmi); swastik is a sacred auspicious symbol here and must not be rendered in a way that resembles the Nazi hakenkreuz; avoid naming a specific deity chauki as a product; use 'inspired by Kumaoni aipan geometry'. GI-protected name 'Uttarakhand Aipan' should not be used as a product label. Made by women; attribute accordingly.
motif_vocabulary: Chauki (seat) diagrams: Nav Durga chauki = three horizontal and three vertical lines with a swastik at centre and nine dots
Chamunda Hast chauki = two triangles crossed by two diagonals with a five-pointed star inside a circle, circle ringed by eight lotus petals
Saraswati chauki = five-pointed star with swastik/lamp at centre
Janeu chauki = seven stars within a six-sided figure
Shiv peeth = eight-cornered figure with 12 dots joined by 12 lines
borders of vasudhara (vertical dripped lines), dots, lotus (ashtadal kamal), Lakshmi footprints
traditions.name: Aipan (Kumaoni ritual floor and wall painting)

traditions.cautions: Kolam is a daily ritual offering (to Bhudevi / threshold deities) and is strongly gendered (women's practice); it is shared across Tamil-speaking regions and diaspora, so attribute it to the Tamil tradition rather than a single state. Avoid presenting generated outputs as ritual kolams; use 'inspired by the Tamil kolam tradition'. Do not combine with deity imagery.
motif_vocabulary: Closed looping curves drawn around a lattice of dots (pulli)
in sikku kolam one or more continuous lines encircle every dot and cross 'over and under'
line kolams join adjacent dots into geometric figures (stars, lotuses, lamps).
traditions.name: Kolam (pulli / sikku kolam)

traditions.cautions: Kolam is not unique to Puducherry; it is the Tamil tradition practised in a UT with a Tamil majority (Puducherry and Karaikal) and should be framed as 'inspired by kolam as drawn in Puducherry', not as a distinct Puducherry craft. Ritual/offering context and women's practice as for Tamil Nadu. The UT's own registered GIs (Villianur Terracotta Works, Thirukannur Papier Mache) are figurative, not geometric.
motif_vocabulary: Overlapping geometric patterns of closed curves drawn around dot grids

traditions.cautions: Ritual art tied to Hindu pujas, births, sacred-thread and marriage rites and to specific deities (Nav Durga, Saraswati, Shiva, Lakshmi); swastik is a sacred auspicious symbol here and must not be rendered in a way that resembles the Nazi hakenkreuz; avoid naming a specific deity chauki as a product; use 'inspired by Kumaoni aipan geometry'. GI-protected name 'Uttarakhand Aipan' should not be used as a product label. Made by women; attribute accordingly.
motif_vocabulary: Chauki (seat) diagrams: Nav Durga chauki = three horizontal and three vertical lines with a swastik at centre and nine dots
Chamunda Hast chauki = two triangles crossed by two diagonals with a five-pointed star inside a circle, circle ringed by eight lotus petals
Saraswati chauki = five-pointed star with swastik/lamp at centre
Janeu chauki = seven stars within a six-sided figure
Shiv peeth = eight-cornered figure with 12 dots joined by 12 lines
borders of vasudhara (vertical dripped lines), dots, lotus (ashtadal kamal), Lakshmi footprints
traditions.name: Aipan (Kumaoni ritual floor and wall painting)

traditions.cautions: These are Indo-Islamic funerary and religious monuments (Salim Chishti's dargah is an active Sufi shrine where pilgrims tie threads to the jalis). Use 'inspired by Mughal jaali geometry', never reproduce or name a specific shrine screen as the product. Jaali geometry is shared across the Islamic world; do not claim UP-exclusive origin. Many UP jalis (e.g. Taj cenotaph screen) are floral/inlaid rather than purely geometric; brief should target the geometric type.
motif_vocabulary: Regular geometric tilings cut as holes in a solid panel: hexagon/six-pointed-star nets, octagon-and-cross, squares-and-rhombi, interlaced polygons
floral/arabesque jalis also exist (Salim Chishti) but the verifiable target here is the geometric type

traditions.cautions: A GI-protected name: do not label generated output 'Lucknow Chikan'; say 'inspired by Lucknow chikan jaali'. the geometric element is the jaali fill.

traditions.cautions: Ritual art tied to Hindu pujas, births, sacred-thread and marriage rites and to specific deities (Nav Durga, Saraswati, Shiva, Lakshmi); swastik is a sacred auspicious symbol here and must not be rendered in a way that resembles the Nazi hakenkreuz; avoid naming a specific deity chauki as a product; use 'inspired by Kumaoni aipan geometry'. GI-protected name 'Uttarakhand Aipan' should not be used as a product label. Made by women; attribute accordingly.
motif_vocabulary: Chauki (seat) diagrams: Nav Durga chauki = three horizontal and three vertical lines with a swastik at centre and nine dots
Chamunda Hast chauki = two triangles crossed by two diagonals with a five-pointed star inside a circle, circle ringed by eight lotus petals
Saraswati chauki = five-pointed star with swastik/lamp at centre
Janeu chauki = seven stars within a six-sided figure
Shiv peeth = eight-cornered figure with 12 dots joined by 12 lines
borders of vasudhara (vertical dripped lines), dots, lotus (ashtadal kamal), Lakshmi footprints
traditions.name: Aipan (Kumaoni ritual floor and wall painting)

Janeu chauki = seven stars within a six-sided figure
Shiv peeth = eight-cornered figure with 12 dots joined by 12 lines

traditions.cautions: The Nicobarese are a Scheduled Tribe in a restricted-access area and the GI is held by a tribal cooperative; any brief must say 'inspired by plaited pandanus mat structure' and must not claim to be a Nicobari mat or use the names Chatrai/Hileuoi as a product name. The mat has ceremonial use (serving food at festivals, hospitality). Do not extend this to other island communities: nothing from Jarawa, Sentinelese, Onge, Great Andamanese or Shompen material culture is proposed or appropriate.
motif_vocabulary: GI Journal 193: 'The weaving process involves crisscrossing the dried leaves by hand, creating a unique, attractive texture ... with different designs and patterns depending on the mat's intended use'

mats are double-layered, typically 6 x 3 ft, natural brownish colour, no artificial colours. Global InCH: 'light and dark leaves are interwoven to create intricate patterns'. Specific pattern names are not documented in any source fetched.

traditions.cautions: These are Indo-Islamic funerary and religious monuments (Salim Chishti's dargah is an active Sufi shrine where pilgrims tie threads to the jalis). Use 'inspired by Mughal jaali geometry', never reproduce or name a specific shrine screen as the product. Jaali geometry is shared across the Islamic world; do not claim UP-exclusive origin. Many UP jalis (e.g. Taj cenotaph screen) are floral/inlaid rather than purely geometric; brief should target the geometric type.
motif_vocabulary: Regular geometric tilings cut as holes in a solid panel: hexagon/six-pointed-star nets, octagon-and-cross, squares-and-rhombi, interlaced polygons
floral/arabesque jalis also exist (Salim Chishti) but the verifiable target here is the geometric type
traditions.name: Mughal pierced-stone jaali screens of Agra and Fatehpur Sikri

traditions.cautions: Kolam is not unique to Puducherry; it is the Tamil tradition practised in a UT with a Tamil majority (Puducherry and Karaikal) and should be framed as 'inspired by kolam as drawn in Puducherry', not as a distinct Puducherry craft. Ritual/offering context and women's practice as for Tamil Nadu. The UT's own registered GIs (Villianur Terracotta Works, Thirukannur Papier Mache) are figurative, not geometric.
motif_vocabulary: Overlapping geometric patterns of closed curves drawn around dot grids
Sahapedia's Seliamedu documentation likens them to the rhythm of sea-wave formations around Pondicherry
flowers are sometimes placed in the centre.
